specificSourceReads: AuthoringRevisionIdentity.referencedIds collects contexts but not text-token references; missing values are currently passed to hashJson.
GuidedSourceClassifier accepts token secrets by opaque secretId and text plain tokens, but context collection handles variableRef and omits secretRef.
SecretReference is explicitly opaque, and StudioContextContractTest plus context-authoring-valid.json retain vault:// context examples.
StudioVariable separates name from secretId; no current proof establishes a general context URI-to-secret mapping.
VaultStudioReferenceResolver refuses an invalid actual secret name such as a vault:// URI before provider access. Structural context acceptance is not evidence of deployed URI resolution.

scopeDecisions.ruling: REPLAYING_PREFIX is a durable continuation and stable public prefix mode across callbacks; resume the next unconsumed coordinate and transition once to SOURCE_PLAN under the session lock. No prefix bootstrap/proposal/reservation may call either gateway. This implements the model-free boundary already required, with the existing plans route and one owner/browser.

The existing context referenceId remains an opaque authored reference. For a new run, every used reference must have one explicit server-approved declaration identity; freeze the exact referenceId-to-secretId mapping and every referenced plain valueHash. Union canonical text tokens with every supported step/global/default reference, with deterministic de-duplication and ordering. Preserve direct <secret ID> meaning, secret-value exclusion, and existing placement restrictions. Do not ban context secretRef or silently discard it to make incremental comparison succeed.
scopeDecisions.mappingBoundary: An exact declared binding of an opaque referenceId to secretId is an acceptable internal design. Do not infer a secretId from URI suffixes, URI paths, display labels, or similar names; do not treat a historical missing mapping as an identity mapping. Aria/C-int must freeze the authoritative mapping source, uniqueness/kind-conflict rules and closed missing/ambiguous refusal before implementation. Syntactic context examples remain valid authoring; unresolved runtime references fail explicitly rather than being ignored.
scopeDecisions.historicalPolicy: Read the base from immutable revision data only. Missing declaration/hash/snapshot metadata means reuse cannot be proven. Refuse incremental reuse with an explicit full-relearn remedy; never null-hash, read live draft variables for the base, backfill guessed history, or silently claim unchanged READY from missing identity. An explicitly requested full learn from step 1 may create a new complete revision. Dev-DB recreation is a separate root/user action and is not authorized here.

scopeDecisions.ruling: One session/context/browser and recording may acquire a bounded append-only materialization version after suffix SOURCE_PLAN. Every existing inputId, value and provenance entry stays byte-identical within that session history. Preserve verified base prefix inputId/bindingId while recapturing fresh values and new-session proof; never reuse old values/admissions/authorization as current evidence. New suffix inputs are appended under collision-safe server IDs. Each preparation/publication/secret lineage joins the version actually used, not the latest row by assumption.

Attribute producer-local binding semantics to producedBindings at the producer step and each semantic edge to consumedBindings at its consumer step. Full learnedPlanHash must still commit and the verifier must check the entire graph. Keep exact ephemeral-field exclusions only; retain operationHash, sourceInputId and all remaining semantic fields. This changes the T0 projection detail, not the first-authored-change boundary or byte-identical prefix promise.
scopeDecisions.example: Changing/deleting a step-4 consumer of a step-2 binding must leave step-2 snapshot byte-identical, keep k=4, and change/omit the step-4 edge only in the new graph. Moving k to step 2, copying stale consumers or dropping edge commitments globally is rejected.
scopeDecisions.reuseProof: Every reusedFrom entry names the immediate pinned base, same test/CSI and same step; keys are exactly the actually replayed contiguous prefix. No j-or-later step is marked reused after drift even if its resulting hash happens to equal the base.

scopeDecisions.ruling: A spent command/admission is immutable and is never sent again. A trusted, authenticated pre-native-invocation target/observation refusal may produce an immutable no-invocation receipt, followed by a fresh learned alternative for the still-unperformed semantic operation. This does not repeat an already-executed browser action. Preserve every successful earlier operation, including earlier ordinals in drift step j; learn only the remaining obligations in that step and all later steps.
scopeDecisions.strictBoundary: A new admission ID is not permission to retry a possibly effected action. Native invocation started, invocation status unknown, lost acknowledgement, assertion FAIL and POLICY_REFUSED remain terminal and cannot manufacture no-invocation proof. Validate proof against current owner/fence/session/coordinate/operation identity through the trusted runner path; model/client claims and absence of a success receipt are insufficient.
scopeDecisions.publication: Exactly one effective executed semantic action per coordinate; every omitted spent attempt has authenticated no-invocation proof and remains committed by publicationEvidenceHash. Preserve successful execution provenance separately. Reject unproven excluded failures, hidden renumbering and replayed earlier effects.

scopeDecisions.ruling: Strict tail deletion selects the last surviving current-draft step as k. Base 1..10 to draft 1..9 replays 1..8 and learns 9 before publishing the shorter revision. A one-step remainder means k=1 and an empty reused prefix. Delete-all may leave an empty draft, but learning refuses before any session/budget/publication write. Omitted firstLearnStepId means server computation, never an end sentinel. READY without an explicit relearn request uses ordinary replay; READY with a valid explicit N uses the same mixed mechanism.
scopeDecisions.emptySuffixDecision: REJECTED for this resumed delta. A zero-suffix/publish-only path contradicts the existing T0 last-surviving-step ruling and is neither required nor authorized. Do not add null/end-sentinel semantics or silently finalize the old revision.
